rounds.question: Name a cause of the Great Depression

answers.explanation: This is a cause of the Great Depression — the October crash wiped out billions in paper wealth, triggering a cascading financial collapse.
This is a cause of the Great Depression — farmers were already struggling through the 1920s before the Depression deepened the crisis.
This is a cause of the Great Depression — investors bought stocks on thin margins; when prices fell, the debts couldn't be repaid.
This is a cause of the Great Depression — over 9,000 banks failed in the 1930s, erasing the savings of millions of ordinary Americans.
This is a cause of the Great Depression — retaliatory tariffs from other nations collapsed international trade and deepened the slump.

rounds.question: Name a hardship Americans faced during the Great Depression

answers.explanation: This is a Depression hardship — by 1933, 25% of American workers were unemployed, with millions more underemployed.
This is a Depression hardship — drought and poor farming practices turned the Great Plains into a wasteland, displacing 'Okies' to California.
This is a Depression hardship — FDR's first act was a bank holiday to stop the panic; millions had already lost everything.
This is a Depression hardship — shantytowns of unemployed men sprang up across the country, named mockingly for President Hoover.
This is a Depression hardship — falling prices sounds good, but it meant farmers couldn't cover costs and businesses couldn't earn profit.

rounds.question: Name a New Deal program and its purpose

answers.explanation: This is a New Deal program — the WPA employed millions to build roads, bridges, parks, and public murals during the Depression.
This is a New Deal program — it created the retirement safety net that still exists today, funded by payroll taxes.
This is a New Deal program — federal deposit insurance ended bank runs by guaranteeing customers wouldn't lose their savings.
This is a New Deal program — young men planted trees, built trails, and worked in national parks for food, shelter, and small wages.
This is a New Deal program — the Securities and Exchange Commission was created to prevent the speculation and fraud that caused the crash.

rounds.question: Name a criticism of FDR's New Deal

answers.explanation: This is a New Deal criticism — conservatives argued deficit spending would saddle future generations with debt.

answers.text: Too much federal power and control
answers.explanation: This is a New Deal criticism — the Supreme Court struck down several programs as unconstitutional overreach of federal power.

answers.text: Did not do enough for Black Americans
answers.explanation: This is a New Deal criticism — many programs allowed racial discrimination; the AAA actually pushed Black sharecroppers off land.
This is a New Deal criticism — FDR's attempt to add six justices to the Supreme Court alarmed even his Democratic allies.
This is a New Deal criticism — unemployment remained above 14% through 1940; only WWII military spending ended the Depression.

rounds.question: Name a way FDR expanded the role of the federal government

answers.explanation: This is how FDR expanded federal government — Social Security, unemployment insurance, and welfare programs permanently changed the government's role.
This is how FDR expanded federal government — the WPA, CCC, and PWA made Washington a direct employer of millions.

answers.text: Regulated banks and the stock market
answers.explanation: This is how FDR expanded federal government — the FDIC and SEC created permanent federal oversight of the financial industry.
This is how FDR expanded federal government — direct relief to unemployed citizens was a radical departure from Hoover's laissez-faire approach.
This is how FDR expanded federal government — his first 100 days set a precedent for presidential leadership in domestic policy.

rounds.question: Name something the US did to move away from isolationism before WWII

answers.explanation: This is how the US moved away from isolationism — FDR lent war materials to Britain without requiring immediate payment.
This is how the US moved away from isolationism — it allowed Allies to buy American arms if they transported them on their own ships.

answers.text: FDR called for being Arsenal of Democracy
answers.explanation: This is how the US moved away from isolationism — FDR's fireside chat framed supplying the Allies as a patriotic duty.
This is how the US moved away from isolationism — earlier laws had barred selling arms to any warring nation; repeal allowed Allied aid.
This is how the US moved away from isolationism — FDR and Churchill's 1941 joint declaration outlined war aims before the US even entered.
